text: i
Checks whether the puzzle is impossible, unique, or non unique.
note: Shows when you click the i next to "Solver".

text: The solver decides the puzzle by finding the correct state for every edge (link or wall). Either by deduction logic, by going neighbors to neighbors, or by testing links between far away symbols. The global idea being that a puzzle solvable by deduction would have a breakthrough spot. The solver is designed to find it by attacking the puzzle with those approaches.
note: Shows when you click the i next to "Solver".

text: If it can't find a breakthrough in the current puzzle state, the solver skips to a final solve and does an exhaustive search on the half done puzzle, hopefully finding an impossibility or a solution. If the solver has trouble finding a solution after a minute of exhaustive search, the puzzle probably requires a global thinking that the solver can’t find. If that is the case, please send your puzzle to me! (nittneuk on discord) so I can try to implement a reasoning for puzzle of it's kind.
note: Shows when you click the i next to "Solver".

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Lines anchor the copy. When both sides have a closed straight line of the same length and one side can not make a second one, the copy must send line onto line: only 4 ways are left (two directions, two mirrors). text: Sizes push each other. A piece smaller than a 3 is 1 or 2 tiles. A chain a < b < c < d makes d at least 4 tiles (5 with a Minimum of 2). A loop a < b < c < a is impossible.

text: 2 and 3. A 2 is exactly two walls. A 3 is three walls, or four if one piece wraps round the corner; when no piece can wrap (too small, or no way round), a 3 with three walls known links the fourth.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Outline and inward corners. Only two tiles touch an outline corner: a 1 links them, a 2 walls them, a 3 or 4 is impossible. Three tiles touch an inward corner (next to a hole or a notch in the board): a 3 there is three walls.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Palisade
What logic was added for Palisade
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: A palisade gives how many of its tile's four sides are walls (0 to 4, a 2 straight or bent). The board edge and empty tiles count as walls.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Count the sides. Once enough sides are known the rest follow: a 1 with its wall found links the other three, a 1 on the outline links its three inner sides.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Size of the piece. A tile with k open sides is in a piece of at least k + 1 tiles: a 0 needs 5, so a 0 with Maximum 4 is impossible. A tile with one open side can end a piece but never let it pass through.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Palisades together. Palisades side by side or corner to corner are solved together: a 0 next to a 3 makes their shared side the 3's only opening, so its other three sides are walls.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Inside a known shape. A polyomino, a bank shape or a rectangle must give each palisade inside it the right count: with Boxy a 0 can only be an inner tile of a rectangle.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Only two pieces. When only two pieces can exist, a straight 2 puts the tiles on its two walled sides in the same piece, and a bent 2 puts the tiles on its opposite sides in different pieces.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Compass
What logic was added for Compass
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: A compass gives how many tiles of its piece lie north, east, south and west of it (over the whole piece, not just its row or column).
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: A count is a limit. With 2 east, nothing three columns or more to the east can join, and a 0 closes its side. A detour round a wall costs tiles too, so a tile the piece can not afford to reach gets a wall.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: The only way. If the piece can only get enough tiles on a side through one tile, that tile joins. Tiles in every piece that fits all the numbers are linked, tiles in none are walled off.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Size. Four numbers cap the piece at 1 + N + E + S + W tiles, and the numbers also give a smallest size: one number k needs k + 1 tiles.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Two compasses. An upper compass with 3 north and a lower one with 1 north can not be one piece: everything north of the upper one is also north of the lower one. Two compasses that would need more tiles apart than the board has on one side are one piece.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Size limits
Precision
What logic was added for Precision
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Every piece has exactly this many tiles.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: The board must divide. 7 tiles with Precision 3 is impossible, and so is every area closed off by walls that is not a multiple. An area of exactly 3 tiles is one piece.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Grow and stop. A group under the size with one way out takes it, and a group at the size is walled all round: on a 1x9 strip with Precision 3 both walls are found at once.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: One connection. Where part of the board hangs on a single edge, counting decides it: 24 tiles behind one edge with Precision 5 need a piece to cross it, so the edge is a link. This works for every size rule.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Minimum
What logic was added for Minimum
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Every piece has at least this many tiles.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Sizes that fit. 7 tiles with Minimum 3 can only use pieces of 3, 4 or 7: a 5 or a 6 would leave 2 or 1 tiles.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Too small. A group under the Minimum with one way out takes it, and one that can not reach enough tiles is impossible. A closed area under twice the Minimum is one piece.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Together with the other bound. A Minimum and a Maximum make a range: 13 tiles with pieces of 4 to 6 can only use 4s and 5s, and a 2x3 board with pieces of 3 to 5 is two pieces of 3.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Maximum
What logic was added for Maximum
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Every piece has at most this many tiles. On its own it says little; it matters with walls, clues or a Minimum.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Too big together. Two groups that would be too big together get a wall. A closed area needs at least (tiles / Maximum) pieces: 10 tiles with Maximum 5 and only two groups make each group its own piece.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Piece rules
Shape bank
What logic was added for Shape bank
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Every piece is one of the bank's shapes (turned or flipped).
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Sizes. Only the bank's sizes count: straight trominoes on 7 tiles is impossible, and a domino and a pentomino on 9 tiles is only 2 + 2 + 5. The same holds for every closed area.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Where a shape can go. The solver lists every placement that holds each group, and what they share is decided: straight trominoes on a 1x6 strip find the wall after the third tile.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: What every shape has. If every bank shape contains a 2x2 block, so does every piece: a tile with no room for a 2x2 around it is impossible. The same goes for a bend.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Mismatch
What logic was added for Mismatch
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Every piece has a different shape.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Enough shapes. There is 1 domino, 2 trominoes, 5 tetrominoes... A board that can not be covered with different shapes is impossible, and sizes that can not be used are dropped.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: A shape is used once. Once a piece is the domino, no other piece can be. Two pieces that can only be the two trominoes take both, even before knowing which is which. Two touching area numbers 2 are one piece (there is a single domino).
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Room for the neighbour. A place is dropped if it leaves a neighbour room only for the same shape: a 1x4 gap can not be filled with 1x2s.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Sizes used up. Once both trominoes are used no other piece has 3 tiles, and Inequality and Difference walls carry that further.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Match
What logic was added for Match
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Every piece has the same shape.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: One size. The size divides the board and every area closed by walls: 12 tiles allow 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 12. With one size left, groups grow to it and stop, and a tile that is the only way into a part of the board takes exactly what is left after whole pieces.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: One shape for every group. Every group known to be one piece must fit in the shape: a bent group of 3 and a straight group of 3 rule out size 3. With one shape left, every group needs a place for it, like a polyomino.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Every tile needs the shape. Every tile of the board must be covered by some placement of the shape: a size where no shape can reach every tile (a dead end at the end of a 1-wide arm, a 2x2 pocket) is dropped.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Mingle Shape
What logic was added for Mingle Shape
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Pieces that touch have different shapes.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Neighbours lose a shape. A piece known to be a shape takes it from every piece across a wall: with a bank of a domino and two trominoes, the piece next to a domino has 3 tiles. Two touching pieces known to be the same shape are one piece.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Two shapes. With only two possible shapes, neighbours alternate like a chessboard: an odd loop of walls is impossible, and no corner has exactly three walls.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Size Separation
What logic was added for Size Separation
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Pieces that touch have different sizes.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Neighbours lose a size. With sizes 2 to 4, the piece next to a 2 has at least 3 tiles. Two touching area numbers 2 are one piece.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Two sizes. With only two possible sizes, neighbours alternate like a chessboard: an odd loop of walls is impossible, and no corner has exactly three walls.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Solitude
What logic was added for Solitude
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Every piece holds exactly one symbol (watchtowers do not count).
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: One symbol each. N symbols make N pieces, and two symbols never share one: neighbouring symbols get a wall.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Reaching a symbol. A group with no symbol must grow to one, so a wall that would cut it off from all of them is a link. A closed area with one symbol is one piece.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Boxy
What logic was added for Boxy
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Every piece is a rectangle.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Fill the box. Tiles of one piece fill the box round them: two tiles at opposite corners of a 2x3 link all six.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Walls run straight. A wall can not stop in the open or turn a corner: at each inner corner it runs straight, makes a T or a cross.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Where the rectangle can go. For a piece of known size the solver lists every rectangle that fits, and what they share is decided. A group already shut on one side (wall, hole, board edge) can not grow past it.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Prime sizes. However the size is known (an area number, Difference or Inequality walls, ...), a prime size is a strip: a piece of 7 is a 1x7, and where 7 tiles do not fit across, it runs up and down.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Non-boxy
What logic was added for Non-boxy
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: No piece is a rectangle.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: At least 3 tiles. A single tile and a domino are rectangles, so every piece has 3 tiles or more.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Keep growing. A group that is a rectangle so far is not finished: with one way out, that edge is a link. A closed strip or a small closed box is impossible.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Bricky
What logic was added for Bricky
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: No corner has four walls meeting (a cross).
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Three walls. Three walls at a corner make the fourth a link.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Poking-in corners. Where two walls meet at a right angle pointing into the board (next to a hole), the tile diagonal to it must join one of its two neighbours: it can never be a one-tile piece. Two pieces (or holes) touching only at a corner are impossible.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Placements. A polyomino, bank shape or rectangle that would leave a cross somewhere is dropped.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Loopy
What logic was added for Loopy
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: No corner has exactly three walls (a T). So every corner has 0, 2 or 4 walls, and the pieces can be coloured with two colours, the outside being one of them.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: The outline is linked. Every outline tile is walled from the outside, so outline tiles side by side are one piece (the same round holes), and a one-tile piece can never sit there.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Three walls. Three walls at a corner make the fourth a wall.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Two colours. A chain of known edges tells whether two tiles have the same colour: same colour gives a link, different a wall. Three pieces that all touch each other are impossible.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Combined rules
Mismatch + few shapes
What logic was added for Mismatch + few shapes
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: With Mismatch and only a few shapes to go round (Boxy, or small pieces), the solver tracks which piece can take which shape.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Shapes taken. Four pieces that can only be the 1x1, 1x2, 1x3 and 1x4 take all four, and every other piece loses them.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Size walls. With few shapes available from the size limits, Difference and Inequality walls become very valuable to tell which small pieces are still available.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Match + pocket of knowledge
What logic was added for Match + pocket of knowledge
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: With Match every piece has the same shape, so whatever a clue tells about its own piece holds for every piece.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Small facts, big picture. Testing every shape of a size one by one is too slow. Instead the solver gathers small facts about the piece from the clues and lets each one cut the list: one fact allows only straight pieces, another needs a tile with all four neighbours in the piece, and together no shape is left.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Reducing size. Some facts keep the piece in a small area, which caps its size: a compass with 0 west close to the east wall forces the shape to be thin.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Match + holes
What logic was added for Match + holes
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: With Match a piece can't surround another piece: if the piece contains a hole, it would need to be a hole of the puzzle.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: A hole for every piece. When tiles known to be one piece close a ring around empty tiles, the shape has a hole of that shape. A board with fewer holes than the minimum number of pieces would fail. A link that would create such a scenario is decided to be a wall. This is the reason the O heptomino can't tile a plane.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Compass + Boxy
What logic was added for Compass + Boxy
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: A Boxy compass counts whole rows and columns.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Corners of the rectangle. A compass with a non-0 number to the west and to the north must reach the tile directly west, directly north and diagonally north-west.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Compass + Roses
What logic was added for Compass + Roses
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: A compass piece has only so many tiles on each side, and still has to reach every rose type.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: The way to a rose. A rose that can only be reached through more tiles to the north than the north number allows is out of reach for that piece.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Area numbers + Roses
What logic was added for Area numbers + Roses
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: An area number fixes the size, the roses fix what the piece must hold.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Every place of the piece. With few pieces the solver lists every place of the numbered piece; the rest of the board must still hold full rose sets.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Close enough. A rose only counts as reachable when the piece plus the way there fits in the number.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: Gemini + Delta
What logic was added for Gemini + Delta
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Gemini says same shape, Delta says different shape.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Never the same two pieces. If one piece touches both a Gemini and a Delta wall, the pieces across them are different.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

text: One symbol per piece
What logic was added for One symbol per piece
note: Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: With Solitude, roses, or all-different area numbers that fill the board, every tile belongs to exactly one symbol's piece.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Who each tile belongs to. Two touching tiles that can not belong to the same symbol get a wall; two that can only belong to the same one get a link. A tile too far from a symbol for its size can not belong to it.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Minimums fill the board. When the smallest pieces of all symbols add up to the board, every piece is that small: 20 compasses that each need 5 tiles on 100 tiles make every piece 5.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: With Boxy. Every rectangle a piece can still be must hold what it needs: a strip along the edge that does not reach all the roses it needs must grow wider to reach them. With Solitude, a rectangle with no symbol is dropped.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule.

note: Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page). Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: No piece may contain a banned shape (turned or flipped).
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule. Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page).

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Contains means inside. Banning the 2x2 bans the P pentomino too. Two groups whose union would hold a banned shape get a wall: with a banned domino every edge is a wall.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule. Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page).

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Biggest allowed piece. If every shape of some size holds a banned shape, no piece can be that big: a banned domino makes every piece one tile. Bank shapes and polyominoes that hold one can not be used.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule. Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page).

text: What logic was added for Wally
note: Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page). Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Every tile needs at least 2 neighbours that are not in its piece; the board edge and holes count as such neighbours. That is the same as: no piece may contain a T tetromino.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule. Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page).

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: At most 2 neighbours inside. A tile can have at most 2 neighbours in its own piece, so once it has 2 links, its other sides are walls. Pieces stay thin: no T, no plus, no 2x2 with a tile sticking out.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule. Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page).

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Placements. A polyomino, bank shape or rectangle that holds a T is dropped: with Boxy every piece is a strip or a 2x2 block.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule. Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page).

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Gemini lines. The two pieces of a Gemini wall have the same straight lines. If one side holds 4 tiles in a line and the other side can not get a new line of 4 anywhere (every try is refuted), the 4 must be the twin of a line the other side already has: next to a closed line of 5, it grows by exactly one tile.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule. Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page).

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Two ends per piece. Every piece is a path with two ends (a tile with 3 walls), a ring, or a single tile. A piece never gets a third end, and once both its ends are known every other tile goes through. With two rose types and every rose a dead end (or Solitude with dead-end symbols), the ends are all used up: every piece starts and ends at its roses.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule. Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page).

text: Heterogeneous
note: Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page).

text: What logic was added for Heterogeneous
note: Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page). Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: Every piece has a different size.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule. Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page).

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: Fewer pieces. Different sizes add up fast: 4 pieces need at least 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 tiles, so a board of 9 tiles has at most 3 pieces. A board that can not be split into different sizes (6 tiles with Precision 3) is impossible.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule. Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page).

kind: text (keep the <b>/<i> tags or drop them)
text: A size is used once. Once a piece is finished, no other piece can have its size. Touching pieces differ in size too, so everything Size Separation finds applies as well.
note: Shows when you click the i next to this rule. Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page).

note: Only shows when custom rules are on (button at the bottom of the page). Not shown on screen: read out by screen readers (it names the control for them).

text: A link joins two tiles: they are in the same piece. It is the opposite of a wall.
